title: Pretension a cobot's dress-pack hose two links and latch its protector at the exit
instruction: Pretension the dress-pack hose two links and latch its protector on it at the retraction unit's exit, then let go of both and move the grippers clear.
context: Robots are dressed with cable packs by hand when they are installed and at each tool change. igus's assembly instructions for its triflex RSE retraction system say to pretension the system by pulling the triflex forward two links and installing a protector at the exit of the moving end: the protector, wider than the exit, then rests on it and keeps the hose two links out. A robot that can do this step can dress and re-tool other robots, one of the manual steps between building a robot and putting it to work. Two arms: the unit's elastic band pulls the hose back (about 4 N two links out here), so the hand that pulls it cannot let go to close the protector. One hand holds the hose out while the other closes and latches the protector on it.
setup: Millimetres; x forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, y left, z up from the table. A parked cobot forearm lies across the table in front of both arms: a grey 63 mm tube, axis at x 250, z 40, from y -215 to 300, on two stands; at its -y end a blue wrist housing, a tool flange and a two-finger tool, all fixed. On top lies its dress pack. The hose is an igus triflex R TRE.40 (43 mm across, 13.9 mm links), modelled as 6.9 mm crests 43 mm across and 7 mm waists 35 mm across, axis at z 101, 120 g, on 8 mm saddles; its moving end, free, is at y -120. Its +y end runs into the exit end of an igus triflex RSE(C) TR.RSE.40 linear retraction unit: an orange 67 x 67 mm housing on the forearm from y 160 to 270 with a 47 mm passage, its exit face at y 160. The hose slides along y only; pulling it toward the wrist (-y) stretches the unit's band, 144 N/m from 0 (4.0 N at 27.8 mm, an estimate: igus give no force), to a stop at 60 mm. At the exit sits an igus TR.40.30 quick-release protector, open, placed round the hose: loose, 30 g, a 55 x 55 mm square shell 27 mm long (y 129 to 156, 4 mm short of the exit face), 5 mm walls, 1 mm clear of the crests, in a cradle fixed on the forearm so it slides along y only: a flat floor 71 mm wide from y 99 to 160, its top at z 73 (0.5 mm under the protector), with a 6 x 12 mm side guide along each edge, 1.5 mm outside the protector's sides (a printed or bent-sheet part in a real trial). Its lid, 55 x 27 x 5 mm, is hinged along y at its +x top edge (x 277.5, z 126) and stands open 95 deg on its stop; a spring of 0.08 N m per rad pushes it open. Under the lid's middle is a rib 3 mm wide and 4.5 mm deep. Pushed shut over a crest, the rib stops the lid about 8 deg open; over a waist it shuts, and within 2.5 deg of shut its quick-lock catches and holds it shut. A waist lies under the rib with the hose out 33.8 mm (and every 13.9 mm from there: 6.0, 19.9, 47.7). Shut there and let go, the hose runs back 6 mm (the rib's 2 mm play, then the protector onto the exit face) and stays 27.8 mm, two links, out. The yellow band is one crest, y 152.0 to 158.9 at the start, beside the open protector; set, it lies just outside the protector's -y face. The hose and forearm have friction 1.0.
scoring: Pull is how far the hose has slid out of the unit (the band's travel toward the wrist); the mark is two links, 27.8 mm. The lid is shut when it is within 2.5 deg of shut (its free edge within 2.4 mm of its shut place); a lid held up by its rib on a crest is about 8 deg open, not shut. A gripper is clear when its axis (the line midway between its finger pads), over the last 38 mm of the fingers, is at least R + 40 mm from the hose and from the protector; R is the distance from that axis to a pad's outer corner (16 mm closed, 57 mm fully open). Score: 0.25 if at some time the pull was within 7 mm (half a link) of the mark. 0.5 if at some time the lid was shut while the pull was within 7 mm of the mark. 0.75 if at the end the lid is shut and the pull is within 5 mm of the mark. 1.0 if, for every moment of the last 1 s, the lid is shut, the pull is within 5 mm of the mark, both grippers are clear and the hose moves under 2 mm/s. Each trial gets the highest tier it meets. A gripper that cannot be read is not clear. Doing nothing scores 0; the lid cannot shut without a pull; setting the hose one link out (shut at 19.9 mm) or three links out (47.7 mm) scores 0. Real trial: a caliper from the exit face to the band's wrist-side edge (8 mm at the start, 35.8 mm at the mark), a 2.4 mm feeler under the lid's free edge, the quick-lock's click, a spring scale on the hose for the band's pull, and top and side video for the grippers.
reset_notes: Open the protector's quick-lock and stand the lid open on its stop. Let the hose run back into the unit to its stop (the band's crest at y 152.0 to 158.9), its free end at y -120. Slide the protector to 4 mm short of the exit face (y 129 to 156). Move both grippers to their ready pose.
fidelity: Simplified: the hose is one rigid run of crests and waists on a straight slide (it cannot bend or sag), and the unit's elastic band is one linear spring of estimated stiffness; only the unit's exit end is modelled. The TR.40.30 is a square shell with a flat lid and one rib, and its quick-lock is a rule. The forearm is a fixed tube. From igus: the step, the parts named, the TRE.40's 43 mm and 13.9 mm links, the protector's 55 x 27 mm.
